title: SQL COUNT: Why Your Report Misses Rows
viewer_problem: Unexpected result from a real software operation
viewer_promise: See the actual operation and verify its effect

beats.spoken_purpose: Why did the report miss records?
Our local table contains records with and without numbers. We want to count every record that arrived, not just those that contain a number. Look at the missing values in the table.
Counting a column skips missing values. The other records still exist in the table, even though the count is smaller.
To count every record, use the star form shown on screen. It counts rows even when a value is missing. Subtract the column count from the row count to find the missing values.
The result shows the total records, the recorded values and the missing values. We check the actual results against the original data.
Both forms are useful. Use the row count for records received and the column count for values recorded. Choose the measure your report needs.
